results.text: When a bank change coincides with a line-down budget overrun, the standard procurement process is overridden to allow immediate PO release (EXPEDITE_PO) while holding payment (HOLD_PAYMENT) until bank callback (VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK) and controller sign-off (ADD_CONTROLLER_SIGNOFF) are completed, supported by line-down evidence (ATTACH_LINE_DOWN_EVIDENCE) and an allowed budget variance (ALLOW_BUDGET_OVERRUN). This procedure was applied in case PR-2026-0312.

08a07221-09fa-46cb-82e7-a31c29cd8207.text: Case PR-2026-0312 involved a procurement exception for ₹4,10,000 for coolant pump assemblies from vendor V-031 due to a recent bank change and a 7% budget overrun in cost centre CC-MACH. | When: 2026-03-11 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops) | Line 3 was stopped due to a lack of parts.

metadata.outcome: line restarted; payment released after callback

1b695ab4-0853-4c10-a1c4-a4199fbfb3d0.text: The standard process was bypassed because holding the PO for a bank callback would have kept line 3 down, and a PO is not a payment. | When: 2026-03-11 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops)

2e9590d2-ecce-4aa4-a976-741a8e536c31.text: The lesson learned is that when a bank change coincides with a line-down budget overrun, the PO should be released while the payment is held until the callback is confirmed.
